children: reported weaker third-quarter distributable earnings Thursday, but shares climbed 5.26% to $115.34 at approximately 11:57 a.m. ET. Investment exits slowed. Investors nevertheless pushed the stock higher as fundraising and recurring fees offered a brighter picture.

According to Reuters, distributable earnings dropped 13% to $1.32 per share, while net realizations slid 34% to roughly $332 million. The counterweight was more than $63 billion in net inflows, lifting assets under management to $1.37 trillion. Fee-related earnings rose 6%, providing some cushion against weaker investment-sale profits.

The valuation chart puts the shares 33.16% below the $172.57 GF Value estimate, suggesting a potential discount rather than guaranteeing upside. The rally is consistent with investors looking past sluggish exits toward a larger fee-generating asset base. Now Blackstone needs to turn more investments into realized profits while keeping fresh capital flowing in.

title: Blackstone Stocks Rally 5.3% as Inflows Cushion Exit Slump
